Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph FEB 19 2020 OILG OPINION NO. MARISSA Q. PADIRAYON Vice-Mayor, Municipality of Sanchez Mira, Province of Cagayan Dear Vice-Mayor Padirayon: s. 202 This has reference to your letter dated 06 January 2020 seeking for this Department's legal opinion regarding certain purchases of parcels of land made by the local chief executive on behalf of the municipal government. To give a background, On 30 June 2019, pursuant to DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2019-39, Mr. Carlito T. Hipolito, Municipal Local Government Operations Officer, entrusted a checklist Of LGU related documents to the office of the Vice- Mayor. Then On 26 Septemeber 2019 said documents were turned over from the Office of the Mayor to the Legislative Office. Upon perusal of the documents, Vice- Mayor Padirayon noticed that the corresponding Sangguniang Bayan Resolution and Ordinance were lacking in some transactions involving the purchase of lots by the LGU. Consequently, Vice-Mayor Padirayon issued a Memorandum dated dated 04 November 2019 addressed to Mr. Joel Puzon, Sangguniang Bayan Secretary, Municpality of Sanchez Mira, Cagayan requesting for certified true copies of the duly approved Sangguniang Bayan Resolution and Ordinance specifically: I. Authority to enter into a Memorandum of Agreement pertaining to the acquisition of a portion of the Real Estate Property of the Heirs of Claudio Caoagas xxx with Transfer Certificate Title No. 191 (TCT No. T-191); and 2. Authority to allocate funds on the purchase of the aforementioned lot. In a Memorandum dated 08 November 2019, Mr. Joel Puzon stated that as per record, Resolution/Ordinance do not exist. However, Sangguninang Bayan Members have expressed their willingness and agreed to issue a Sangguniang Bayan Resolution/Ordinance in order to cure the defect of the contract entered by the LGU through Honorable the Mayor. In addition, at the time of the sale of TCT No. T-191, what was provided by the Heirs of Claudio Caoagas to the LGU was a mere photocopy of the Title. Moreover, the sale was consummated on 04 August 2017 when the payment was made, but on 09 August 2017, a certain Dina Nicandro filed an Affidavit of Loss of TCT No. T -191 and was thereafter issued a new Title by the Register of Deeds on November 2018 and is still currently in her possession. Further, TCT No. T- 191 is the mother Title of the other three (3) lots which was purchased by the LGU.

Under this premise arose the request for clarification regarding the propriety of the purchase of certain parcels of land by the Municipality of Sanchez Mira. Accordingly, the request submitted for this Department's legal opinion are hereunder presented: 1. Acquisition of the LGU ofa parcel of land through Deed of Absolute Sale without a Sangguniang Bayan Resolution/Ordinance for that matter; 2. Amending the Resolution No. 2017-068, A Resolution Granting Authority to the Honorable Asela B. Sacramed, Municipal mayor, To Represent the Municipal Government of Sanchez Mira in the Purchase of Lot Through Deed of Absolute Sale With the Carillo Family, dated 17 July 2017, to specifically indicate therein the details of the four (4) Deed of Self- Adjudication and Sale of Registered Land transactions involving four (4) parcels of land purchased by the Municipality of Sanchez Mira, which are still included and covered by TCT No. T-191 3. The Title that was presented during the sale was a mere photocopy; and 4. It was not specified in the Appropriation Ordinance the aforementioned transactions. Primarily, please be advised that this Department shall focus on generalities to avoid encroaching upon the prerogatives and jurisdiction of the courts as the queries submitted are justiciable in nature and would require a determination of the legality or validity of actions of both the local chief executive and the Sangguniang Bayan based on the facts alleged in the letter and the applicable law thereto. Considering that the issues are interrelated, this Department deems it appropriate to tackle the matter in one discussion. To begin with, it is imperative to cite the pertinent provisions of Republic Act No. 7160 otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991, as amended (LGC), to wit: SECTION 22. Corporate Powers. - (a) Every local government unit, as a corporation, shall have the following powers: (c) Unless otherwise provided in this Code, no contract may be entered into by the local chief executive in behalf of the local government unit without prior authorization by the sanggunian concerned. A legible copy of such contract shall be posted at a conspicuous place in the provincial capitol or the city, municipal or barangay hall. " "SECTION 444. The Chief Executive: powers, Duties, Functions and Compensation. - xxx (b) For efficient,

effective and economical governance the purpose of which is the general welfare of the municipality and its inhabitants pursuant to Section 16 of this Code, the municipal mayor shall: (1) Exercise general supervision and control over all programs, projects, services, and activities of the municipal government, and in this connection, shall: (vi) Upon authorization by the sangguniang bayan, represent the municipality in all its business transactions and sign on its behalf all bonds, contracts, and obligations, and such other documents made pursuant to law or ordinance; Relatedly, as mentioned in the letter, the case of Quisumbing v. Garcial is instructive as to the authority of the local chief executive to enter into contracts on behalf of the LGU, wherein the Supreme Court made a pronouncement that the local chief executive must inquire if the provisions in the appropriation ordinance specifically cover the expense to be incurred or the contract to be entered into. Correspondingly, in the latter case of Verceles Jr., v. Commission on Audit2, the High Court reiterated its ruling in the Quisumbing case, to wit: "The prior authorization for the local chief executive to enter into contracts on behalf of the local government unit may be in the form of an appropriation ordinance passed for the year which specifically covers the project, cost, or contract to be entered into by the local government unit. If the project or program is identified in the appropriation ordinance in sufficient detail, then there is no more need to obtain a separate or additional authority from the sanggunian. In such case, the project and the cost are already identified and approved by the sanggunian through the appropriation ordinance. To require the local chief executive to secure another authorization for a project that has been specifically identified and approved by the sanggunian is antithetical to a responsive local government envisioned in the Constitution and in the LGC. On the other hand, the need for a covering contract arises when the project is identified in generic terms. The covering contract must also be approved by the sanggunian. " Therefore, in view of the foregoing, this Department is of the considered view that as a general rule, prior authorization from the Sangguniang Bayan is necessary 1 G.R. No. 175527, December 8, 2008. 2 G.R. NO. 211553, September 13, 2016.

in order for the local chief executive to enter into contracts in behalf of the municipality except separate prior authorization is no longer required, if the specific projects are covered by appropriations in the annual budget of the LGU. The appropriation ordinance passed by the Sanggunian is the local chief executive's authority to enter into a contract implementing the project. As to your second query, this Department is of the opinion that there is no need to amend Resolution No. 2017-068 to specifically indicate the details regarding the parcels of land purchased by the municipality that are covered by Transfer Certificate No. 191 considering that Resolution No. 2017-068 already grants authority to the Municipal Mayor to represent the municipal government in the purchase of lot through Deed of Absolute Sale and that funds have been appropriated for such purpose. Hence, so long as the local chief executive has been granted authority by the sanggunian to enter into a contract on behalf of the local government unit, sufficiently complies with the requirement under the law. Further, as to your third query, possession of the original or certified true copy of the Transfer Certificate of Title, the Deed of Absolute Sale and the other necessary and relevant documents are some of the requirements for the titling of the subject property. Since your fourth query is related to the first, this Department would like to reiterate that the City Mayor is required by law to seek further approval or authorization of the Sanggunian for projects described in generic terms. In contrast, sanggunian authorization may already be contained in the apprpriations ordinance if the same provides sufficient detail the project and the cost of the capital outlay and therefore no further authorization is required as the same complies with Section 22(c) of the Code. Notwithstanding the foregoing, this Department would like to respectfully suggest that the issues presented herein may be brought to our courts of justice for a comprehensive review and appreciation of the facts and for a full determination of the applicable laws to effectively resolve the matter. Thank you. COPY FURNISHED: JONATHAN PAUL M. LEUSEN, JR., CESO 111 Regional Director DILG - Region 11 Regional Government Center Carig Sur, Tuguegarao City, Province of Cagayan LLLS/32 trul ours, M. ANO EDUA Secretary o iLG til OILG,OSEC 02152070-0"
